clue.text: Participate in a hold-up for a health proposal?

definitions.text: Participate in a hold-up for a health proposal?

parts.words: Participate in a hold-up for a health proposal?
parts.note: a 'hold-up' sounds criminal, but here it is lifting a drink in the air while someone proposes a toast to good health

explanation.surface: Someone is being asked to join in an armed robbery, oddly for the sake of wellbeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' pulls toward a robbery; it is literal lifting, and the 'health proposal' is a toast such as 'Your health!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting a drink is how a person joins in a toast, which wishes someone good health.

clue.text: Give an office to ruthless leader switching unequal parts

indicators.note: the leader's name is split into a longer front and a shorter back, and those two pieces swap places

parts.note: Joseph Stalin, the brutal Soviet dictator

explanation.surface: A tyrant is reorganising his bureaucracy, dishing out positions unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching unequal parts' splits STAL|IN and puts IN first.
explanation.definitionFit: To instal (British spelling) someone is to place them formally in a post or office.

clue.text: European, gutted over Greek state, who produces incisive letters

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, so only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A disappointed European sits above a Greek state, alongside a cutting writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' sounds like dismay but strips European to EN; in a down clue 'over' just puts EN above GR.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver cuts lettering into metal or stone, so the letters are literally incised.

clue.text: The reverse of fine and cool?

definitions.text: The reverse of fine and cool?

indicators.note: the pieces that follow are read backwards, last letter first

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
to fan something is to cool it

explanation.surface: Something is described as the opposite of nice and trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, F and FAN give the answer, and the whole clue also defines it: the opposite of fine and cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool, the very opposite of stylish and fine.

clue.text: Saigon cultivated Southern Hemisphere trees

indicators.note: cultivated land is worked over and turned, so the letters are dug up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Plantations around the Vietnamese city grow trees from below the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges SAIGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ngaios are small New Zealand trees, native to the southern half of the globe.

clue.text: Moral expert's ancient letter on one sacred Greek box

parts.note: eth is an Old English letter for the th sound
I is the Roman numeral one
a cist is a chest used for sacred utensils in ancient Greek ritual

explanation.surface: A moral philosopher's old letter rests on a holy Greek casket.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' simply puts the pieces in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethicist is a specialist in moral philosophy and right conduct.

clue.text: Clip the front of light brown beard

indicators.note: clipping the front trims away the opening letter of the word

parts.note: fawn is a pale brown colour

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim the tip of a sandy-coloured beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' wants to be facial hair; it is the botanical sense, a bristly growth on grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: The bristly tufts on ears of barley are called its beard; each bristle is an awn.

clue.text: Audio receivers brought in close, once spread without thinking ahead

indicators.note: one piece is brought inside the other, so it sits within it

parts.note: nigh is an old-fashioned word for close or near
ears receive sound
to ted is to spread out hay for drying

explanation.surface: Hearing devices are moved nearby and laid out carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is a haymaking word, and 'once' marks nigh as archaic. 'brought in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a myopic plan sees only what is close and lacks foresight.

clue.text: Worrying results adapted to cover science fiction

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece, covering it
adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anxious findings are reworked to take in a sci-fi angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' gives STRESUL, which 'to cover' wraps round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stressful causes anxiety and strain, which is to say it is worrying.

clue.text: Hands-free devices jerk constantly, leaving last two in dumps

indicators.note: the jerk and the trimmed word go inside the other piece

parts.note: to ditch is to dump or get rid of
a git is a contemptible fool, British slang

indicators.note: the final pair of letters departs from the word

parts.note: always means constantly

explanation.surface: Gadgets with no hands are twitching nonstop while the end two lie in rubbish heaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands-free' wants to mean phones; it means dials with no hands. 'leaving last two' trims the word for constantly, and 'in' puts both pieces inside the word for dumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Watches with numeric displays have no clock hands, so they are hand-free timekeepers.

clue.text: Oversexed chap has lead, then every third in stray cycling

indicators.text: has lead, then every third in
indicators.note: take the leading letter, then each third letter after it, counting along the run

parts.note: the word stray is written out again and again, going round like a wheel

explanation.surface: A randy man leads, then joins a wandering bicycle ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lead' starts on S; cycling round STRAY repeatedly and taking every third letter gives S, A, T, Y, R.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a satyr is a lustful woodland being, so the word is used for a lecherous man.

clue.text: Ready to excuse six involved in fakery

indicators.note: the number is wrapped up inside the other word

parts.note: forging is faking documents or money
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: Someone is willing to pardon half a dozen people caught up in counterfeiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A forgiving person is inclined to pardon others' faults.

clue.text: Endless Green promises to pay, keeping British in the dark

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the other letter within them
without its end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: olive is a shade of green
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's unending pledges of payment leave a Briton uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the eco-party; it is a colour. 'Endless' gives OLIV, and 'keeping' holds the British letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is to be unaware, which is what oblivious means.

clue.text: Westerner's irrational to replace study that's opposed to 18

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another inside the word

parts.note: an Occidental is a person from the West
a den is a private study
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: A Westerner illogically swaps out his studies for something opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' puts PI where DEN was in OCCIDENTAL. 18 is FRONTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The occipital bone is at the back of the skull, the opposite end from the frontal bone.

clue.text: Hide opening from the poor

parts.note: a hide is an animal skin

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Concealing the start of something from people in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb; it is a noun, an animal's pelt. SKINT is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is British slang for having no money, i.e. broke.

clue.text: Perhaps gutsy type in command

parts.note: to type data into a computer is to enter it
IC stands for in charge, i.e. in command

explanation.surface: A bold sort of person is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutsy' wants to mean brave; here it means relating to the guts.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric means relating to the intestines, so a bowel disorder is one example, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Writer's impulse to stop mounting release of emotions

indicators.note: the impulse plugs the word like a stopper
in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: giving vent to feelings releases them
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: An author feels the need to halt a rising outpouring of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' gives TNEV, read upwards in a down clue; 'to stop' plugs the impulse into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Forward on raft, twisting left

indicators.note: twisted letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Someone on a raft heads forward while veering left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' rearranges ON and RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Frontal describes what is at the front, i.e. forward.

clue.text: E.g. Iceland's brand new stuffing bird, the first to be killed?

indicators.note: the letter is stuffed inside the bird, like a filling

parts.note: an owl is a bird
in Genesis, Abel was the first person murdered

explanation.surface: A supermarket's new product is a stuffed bird, the first one slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceland is a UK frozen-food supermarket chain, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's in-house products are sold under its private brand, like a supermarket's range.

clue.text: Trigonometry about primarily hypotenuse and circumference

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short form is read backwards

parts.note: trig is the usual short form of trigonometry

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the word's first letter is used

explanation.surface: A maths lesson about the hypotenuse and the distance round a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TRIG into GIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement around something, its circumference.

clue.text: The boy had time to become a climber

parts.note: he refers to a boy
'd is the contraction of had
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lad has grown up into a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the genus of ivy, a familiar climbing plant.

clue.text: Rewritten play is one part embracing South Pacific

indicators.note: a rewritten text has its letters set down afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A revised script includes one segment staging the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewritten' rearranges PLAY IS ONE. South Pacific is also a musical, which the play surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the region of Oceania covering much of the central and southern Pacific islands.

clue.text: No English in canal site hospital or in French place on Grand Canal

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Suez is the site of the Suez Canal
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
ou is French for or

explanation.surface: A canal-side hospital without English speakers, or one in a French town on a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No English' drops E from SUEZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Suzhou is a Chinese city on the Grand Canal, the ancient waterway linking Beijing and Hangzhou.

clue.text: Obsessive about City stud from unreliable stories?

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word goes round the others

parts.note: anal means obsessively fussy
EC is the postcode area of the City of London
a dot is a small round spot, like a stud

explanation.surface: A fussy person concerned about a City stallion has dubious tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stud' suggests a horse; it is a small round point.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence comes from personal tales rather than reliable study.

clue.text: Parking facilities must go on ring road, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going on another sits above it

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for the lavatory, the loo
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car park's toilets must be placed on the bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facilities' is the toilet; in a down clue LOO goes on top of P.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a circuit, and a ring road is one example.

clue.text: Unknown amount in a container tipped over digger

indicators.note: the unknown goes inside the other letters
a tipped-over word is upended, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a can is a container
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown quantity spills from a tipped tin onto a mechanical excavator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped over' turns CAN into NAC; Z goes inside. 'digger' looks like a machine; it is slang for an Australian soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Digger is slang for an Australian soldier, and an Anzac is one from the First World War.

clue.text: Metric units are wrong? Maybe pint unit serves country

parts.note: SI is the international system of metric units
to err is to be wrong
a pint of beer is often ale
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A barman questions metric measures while serving a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe pint' is an example definition of ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Be beholden to some ne'er-do-wells

indicators.note: only some of the letters, a run inside the words, are used

explanation.surface: Being indebted to a few layabouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be indebted to someone, i.e. beholden.
